categories.main_business_segments: The Clorox Company operates through four reportable segments: Health and Wellness (cleaning products, professional products, vitamins, minerals, and supplements), Household (bags and wraps, grilling products, cat litter), Lifestyle (food, natural personal care, water-filtration products), and International (products sold outside the U.S. across similar categories). These segments are structured around strategic business units focused on both consumer and professional markets.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Clorox leverages proprietary formulations and manufacturing processes for cleaning, disinfecting, and personal care products, as well as food and water-filtration technologies. The company emphasizes digital transformation, including a major investment in cloud-based enterprise resource planning and digital supply chain enhancements, and uses both in-house and third-party manufacturing.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Clorox primarily serves mass retailers, grocery outlets, warehouse clubs, dollar stores, home hardware centers, drug, pet, and military stores, as well as e-commerce channels and distributors. Its key customers include large retailers such as Walmart (which accounts for 25% of net sales), and it also targets professional customers in institutional, janitorial, food-service, and healthcare sectors.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates globally, with 84% of net sales in the U.S. and 16% from international markets. It maintains a strong presence in North America and has significant operations in Latin America, Canada, Australia, and select other international markets, with leading brands in most countries where it operates.
categories.supply_chain_position: Clorox is primarily a downstream operator, manufacturing and marketing branded consumer and professional products that are distributed through retail and commercial channels. It sources raw materials from a global network of suppliers and manages a complex supply chain to deliver finished goods to end customers.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Clorox’s IGNITE strategy focuses on fueling growth, innovating consumer and customer experiences, reimagining work, and evolving its portfolio. The company is investing heavily in digital transformation, supply chain modernization, and ESG initiatives, with R&D directed at product innovation, sustainability, and digital capabilities.
categories.revenue_model: The company generates revenue primarily through the sale of branded consumer and professional products to retailers, distributors, and direct-to-consumer channels. Revenue streams include product sales across cleaning, household, lifestyle, and international categories, with some licensing and joint venture income (e.g., Glad with P&G).
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Clorox competes in highly competitive markets against major multinational and national consumer products companies, as well as private label and store brands. Its products generally compete on performance, brand reputation, and price, and about 80% of its sales come from brands holding No. 1 or No. 2 market share positions in their categories.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In fiscal year 2022, Clorox reported net sales of $7.1 billion and employed about 9,000 people worldwide. The company experienced a 3% decrease in net sales and a 33% decrease in diluted EPS compared to the prior year, reflecting normalization after pandemic-driven demand spikes and ongoing supply chain and inflationary pressures.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Clorox emphasizes trusted, high-performing brands with strong market positions, focusing on health, wellness, and sustainability. Its value proposition centers on product efficacy, brand recognition, innovation, and a commitment to ESG goals, including renewable energy, reduced packaging waste, and community well-being initiatives.
